want.now.why: will sits in second position and lernen goes to the end: the door and its verb form a bracket around the object.

want.past.why: Tense goes on the door itself: wollte is Präteritum, which is what speakers use for modals even though other verbs take Perfekt.

want.neg.why: No do-support: nicht slips inside the bracket, after the object and just before the infinitive at the end.

want.q.why: Inversion only: the door moves to first position and becomes the question marker; no particle, no do.

decline.now.why: weil sends the conjugated verb (muss) to the end of its clause, so the second door comes after its own verb.

decline.past.why: Both doors take Präteritum (konnte, musste), the spoken past for modals; musste still lands at the end of the weil clause.

decline.fut.why: No substitute needed: können has a future, but speakers just keep the present and let morgen carry the tense. werde ... kommen können is possible but stiff.

decline.although.why: obwohl is subordinating like weil, so the shape is identical: muss goes to the end of clause two.

like.now.why: Straight subject-verb-object, the liker is nominative. Ich trinke gern Kaffee is the other common way to say it.

like.neg.why: Negation fuses with the article: keinen (kein + accusative masculine) replaces nicht before an indefinite noun.

like.she.why: mag is the same for ich and sie: mögen is a modal-type verb with no -t in third person singular.

like.q.why: Verb to first position marks the question; magst carries the du ending -st. No do, no particle.

go.habit.why: Time before place in the middle field: jeden Tag comes before auf den Markt. Accusative den because it is movement.

go.prog.why: No progressive: the same gehe as the habit sentence, with gerade doing the job of both am and now.

go.past.why: Spoken past is the Perfekt: bin in second position, participle gegangen at the very end, everything else in between.

go.fut.why: werde plus infinitive at the end, same bracket as the Perfekt. In speech Ich gehe morgen auf den Markt is more common.

go.neg.why: No aux to hang the negation on: nicht comes after the verb and before the place phrase it negates.

live.now.why: Plain present wohne; the 'have been' meaning lives in seit (dative: Jahren). Time before place again.

live.past.why: Finished period: Perfekt bracket habe ... gewohnt, and the duration is bare accusative zwei Jahre, no seit.

live.fut.why: Present plus schon instead of Futur II; nächstes Jahr in first position pushes ich behind the verb (verb-second).

live.q.why: Question word first, verb second, du third. schon is what turns present wohnst into 'have you been living'.

if.real.why: wenn sends habe to the end of its clause; that clause counts as position one, so verreise comes next and ich follows it. Present, no werde.

if.unreal.why: Konjunktiv II: hätte at the end of the wenn clause, würde in the main clause with verreisen pushed to the end.

if.past.why: Past Konjunktiv II: gehabt hätte stacks at the end of the wenn clause; verreisen takes sein, so it is wäre ... verreist, not hätte.
